topic: Oregon name and/or sex change petition
statement: Oregon lets you ask a circuit court to change your legal name and/or your sex on record through the same petition process. You complete a statewide Name and Sex Change Packet plus a Name Change – Supplemental form, then file them with the court in person or by US mail.
detail: After you file, the court opens a case, reviews your documents, and contacts you about your next step — which may include a hearing before a judge. Minor applicants use a separate, additional packet with its own requirements.

cost.note: This page does not list a filing fee. Contact the circuit court where you file for the current amount.

source.title: Oregon Judicial Department, Lane County Circuit Court — Name Change and/or Sex Change

statement: To change the name on your Oregon driver's license, permit, or ID card, make an appointment or visit a DMV office for standby service, present proof of your legal name change, and present proof of your identity and address, then pay the applicable fee.
detail: DMV verifies your Social Security number with the Social Security Administration, so if you want a REAL ID-compliant credential the name on it must match what SSA has on file — you need to update your name with SSA first. For a standard, non-REAL-ID credential, the name on your card can differ from SSA's records if you provide proof of that name. You can also change your gender marker as part of the same visit.

cost.note: The page says to pay the applicable fee but does not state the amount; see DMV's fee schedule for current pricing.

source.title: Oregon Department of Transportation — Changing Your Name

statement: Oregon offers three gender markers on a driver's license, permit, or ID card — M (male), F (female) or X (not specified) — by self-attestation. You do not need to bring any documents indicating your gender or sex; just bring your current ID and select the marker you want.
detail: You cannot change your gender marker online — you have to make an appointment or visit a DMV office in person. DMV does not require your gender marker to match Social Security Administration records or anything else, and it keeps a history of your prior names and gender markers on file for fraud prevention.

cost.note: You pay the renewal or replacement fee for a new card; the page does not state the amount.

source.title: Oregon Department of Transportation — Changing Your Gender Marker on Your Driver's License or ID Card

statement: People born in Oregon can change the sex on their birth record to M, F, or X (non-binary) to support their gender identity, either by signing a notarized Application to Change the Name and/or Sex on a Record of Live Birth to Support Gender Identity (form OHA 2673) or by getting a court order. The notarized application route, from House Bill 2673, does not require a court order.
detail: Name and sex do not have to be changed at the same time on this form, but each can only be changed once through this administrative process — any further change needs a court order. You must be 18 or older (or an emancipated minor) to apply for yourself; a parent or legal guardian applies for a registrant under 18.

cost.note: The $35 amendment fee does not include a birth certificate copy: a certificate costs $25 (computer-issued) or $30 (full image) each, and an optional $30 fee expedites the amendment itself.

timeline.typical: Standard processing time isn't fixed here — the page points to a separate, weekly-updated list of current processing times. Once your amendment is processed, your new certificate is mailed to you, which takes 7 to 10 business days for delivery unless you arrange your own faster shipping.

source.title: Oregon Health Authority — Changing a Birth Record to Support Gender Identity

statement: To substantially change the name on an Oregon birth certificate — removing part of it or changing it to a new name, not just fixing a typo — Oregon Health Authority requires a court-ordered name change. Oregon vital records will not automatically update your birth certificate just because a court granted a name change; you have to request the amendment yourself.
detail: You submit an original certified copy of the court order (showing the court clerk's original seal and signature), a completed Request to Change Birth Certificate Based on Court Order of Name Change form, a completed Amend a Birth Record Order form, and a copy of your valid photo ID.

cost.note: The amendment fee is $35. Getting a certified copy of the court order itself has its own fee, set by the court, not stated on this page.

source.title: Oregon Health Authority — Change a Birth Record
